notes: THREE independent occurrences in one day, in three different subsystems. The operator observed that this makes it one of the two strongest candidates in the set: the ladder step "applied in another implementation / validated by reuse" is already satisfied by the historical record. Promotion to `validated` is the operator's to make, not an agent's.
Crossing persona scope to key on the subject means returning ONLY the narrow facts asked for — never the receipt body, which stays persona-scoped (Identity & Access Spine, T0).

canaries.assertion: 'queries on the runtime agent id and never looks up a persona row' — asserts the `personas` table is not touched at all; plus 'finds journey receipts by runtimeAgentId, not by the agent’s own persona' and 'no longer resolves the agent’s persona row to find receipts'.
'MarketaEligibilityView requires agentSlug — props are read, not discarded' and 'both the GET refresh and the POST prove-control call send agentSlug — neither can fall back to the server default'.

statement: Actor, subject and owner are distinct references and must never be silently substituted.

occurrences.defect: Receipts were looked up under the registered AGENT's persona; every `horizen_agent_registered` receipt carries personaId = the ACTING operator. The query searched a structurally empty set every time and reported 'not registered'.

The client omitted `agentSlug`, so the server substituted DEFAULT_REGISTRABLE_AGENT_SLUG (MoneyPenny) for the agent the operator had visibly selected. Claim refused with `aigentqube-moneypenny` while claiming Nakamoto.

The `/state` route resolved the AGENT's own persona (`personas.fio_handle = 'nakamoto@aigent'`) and listed its receipts. receiptRefs came back empty, every hasReceipt() was false, and Register could never render COMPLETE however completely it had succeeded.
